subject: Proposed subcontractor scope expansion — action & review
messages:
From: Contracts Team <contracts@cloudsync.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor scope increase & proposed amendment (CloudSync)

Hi Rishi —

Quick heads-up: CloudSync is planning to expand the set of subprocessors they will use to accelerate ingestion for our integration pilot. The new vendors are two EU-based logging processors and one US-based analytics partner. Attached is the proposed amendment ("CloudSync_Subproc_Amendment_v1.docx") and an annotated DPA excerpt.

Highlights:
- New subprocessors will have access to hashed metadata and transient logs (no PII).
- We expect the change to go live 10/01; CloudSync requests our consent by 08/27 to keep timeline.
- They propose flow-down language mirroring our MSA, including a carve-out that allows subprocessor access for debugging.

Can you confirm the path for approval and whether Redwood requires a separate order form change or addendum? Also please let us know if you need additional evidence (SOC / audit reports) — we can pull the most recent artifacts from our portal.

Thanks,
Maya Gomez
Contracts Lead | CloudSync
attachments: CloudSync_Subproc_Amendment_v1.docx, CloudSync_DPA_annotated.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Contracts Team <contracts@cloudsync.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor scope increase & proposed amendment (CloudSync)

Maya —

Thanks for the packet and the timeline. Looping in Ben (Security Ops) and Rishi (Legal/product touchpoint) to coordinate. Quick asks from our side so we can triage internally:

1) Please summarize data categories the new subprocessors will access in a single table (example: hashed session id, customer id pseudonym, logs).
2) Confirm whether CloudSync will act as controller or processor for any transformed data (we need this for DPA analysis).
3) Provide SOC2 Type II or equivalent for the two EU processors; if unavailable, send last three months of system logs and a contact for audit evidence.

On Redwood side: Ben, please scope whether the proposed flow-down language (section 5.3 in the amendment) is acceptable from our security posture or if we need stronger contractual hooks (e.g., explicit encryption at rest obligations and subprocessor vetting terms). Rishi — can Legal confirm whether we need an Order Form amendment vs. a stand-alone consent form? CloudSync is asking us for sign-off by 8/27.

Short replies ok — we need to respond to CloudSync with next steps by EOD 8/24 so they can meet their build schedule.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Third-Party Operations <ops@cloudsync.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor scope increase & proposed amendment (CloudSync)

Hi Lauren/Rishi/Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a brief matrix summarizing the categories (see appended table in CloudSync_DPA_annotated.pdf). For the EU logging partners we can provide SOC2 equivalency (ISO 27001 + penetration test report); for the US analytics partner we can provide SOC2 Type II (Q2 2027).

A couple clarifications:
- Data exposure is limited to hashed session ids and anonymized metrics; no raw user content or credential material will be shared.
- CloudSync remains processor; subprocessors are engaged as subprocessors under our DPA.
- They flagged that Redwood’s standard flow-down requires an additional audit clause; CloudSync proposes a redline in the amendment (section 7.1) allowing on-demand audits with 30 days notice and a limited-scope review.

We also pushed an editable DPA into DocuSign for convenience: https://www.docusign.net/CLDSYNC-12345 (link expires 9/04). If it helps, we can open a temporary view for Redwood security to review raw controls.

Cheers,
Maya

Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Subprocessor scope increase & proposed amendment (CloudSync)

Forwarding CloudSync packet. Key points for Legal/Product:

- Timeline pressure: CloudSync wants yes/no consent by 08/27; realistic internal SLA is EOD 08/24 for our response so they can keep their release.
- Primary concerns: audit access language (section 7.1), the "debugging access" carve-out (section 5.3), and explicit encryption/segregation language for analytics exports.
- Proposed ask: Legal to provide redline suggestions on the amendment and DPA by 08/24 morning; Security (Ben) to confirm whether on-demand audits with 30 days notice is acceptable or requires pushback.

Please reply with: (a) redline doc link or comments, (b) risk classification (low/medium/high) for the three subprocessors, (c) what evidence we will demand before consenting.

Quoted below is the latest CloudSync note for context.

>

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor scope increase & proposed amendment (CloudSync)

Quick update from Security Ops after a 30-min review:

- Risk: medium. EU logging partners have solid controls but the "debugging access" language needs to be narrowed (timebox and purpose).
- Evidence required: SOC2/ISO certs plus a read-only view into their attestation portal; for US analytics partner we want the Q2 SOC2 report and a sample retention schedule.
- Audit clause: we should push to either (a) limit audit scope to control mapping against our standard (not full system access) or (b) require an independent assessor report. 30 days notice is fine but add a clause that audits will be scoped to business hours and fail-safe redaction of customer data.

I will draft suggested redlines to the amendment and upload to our shared Drive by EOD 8/24. Karthik — will you confirm if Procurement needs to issue an Order Form amendment (vs. a separate consent) or if Legal can sign the consent-only route?

Ben Carter
Director, Security Operations | Redwood Inference
